high.title: Ringgit closes marginally higher ahead of FOMC outcome
high.summary: The ringgit traded at 4.0875/4.0915 against the USD as markets awaited the FOMC decision, with geopolitical tensions in West Asia driving crude oil prices up over 3.6%. A hawkish Fed tone could strengthen the USD and pressure the ringgit, making this a critical watch point for Malaysian investors and businesses with USD exposure.

high.title: Ringgit opens higher against greenback on improved local sentiment
high.summary: Malaysia's economy is projected to grow 4%-5% in 2026, likely towards the upper end, boosting local sentiment and supporting the ringgit. The ringgit is expected to hover around RM4.08-RM4.09 ahead of the FOMC decision, with weaker US consumer confidence data suggesting the Fed may hold rates steady, which could benefit the ringgit.

high.title: Bursa ends lower ahead of Fed decision, tech earnings
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia closed lower as investors adopted a wait-and-see approach ahead of the FOMC rate decision and major US tech earnings. Concerns over Nvidia's AI financing commitments exceeding US$750 billion raised questions about the sustainability of the AI-driven rally. Falling Brent crude prices also failed to lift market sentiment.

high.title: Ringgit opens higher against major currencies, eases vs US dollar
high.summary: The ringgit eased slightly against the US dollar to 4.0850/4.0900 as markets anticipated a potential US interest rate rise from the upcoming FOMC meeting on July 28-29. Bank Muamalat's chief economist noted the greenback could strengthen if rates rise, keeping the ringgit-USD pair in a narrow trading range. This directly impacts Malaysian importers, exporters, and currency-sensitive investments.

high.title: Ringgit strengthens ahead of US Fed rate decision
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0835/4.0875 against the US dollar following a significant drop in crude oil prices after the US and Iran halted hostilities. WTI crude fell nearly 7% and Brent crude fell nearly 8%, signalling eased geopolitical risk but with caution as the situation remains fluid. The upcoming FOMC meeting remains the key near-term driver for the ringgit's direction.

high.title: Bursa ends higher on bargain hunting
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia rebounded on bargain hunting as Brent crude fell sharply by nearly 8% to US$89.22 per barrel amid easing West Asia tensions. Analysts maintain a cautious near-term outlook as investors await key US economic data, Big Tech earnings, and the upcoming Federal Reserve policy decision. These factors collectively influence investor sentiment and market direction in Malaysia.

high.title: Oil prices sink as US-Iran pause fuels fresh Hormuz hopes
high.summary: A temporary pause in US airstrikes on Iran and Tehran's halt of retaliatory attacks on regional neighbours has eased Strait of Hormuz tensions, causing Brent crude to drop sharply after breaking above US$100 per barrel last week. The de-escalation has significant implications for Malaysia as an oil-dependent economy and for shipping routes critical to Malaysian trade. Continued geopolitical developments in this corridor will remain a key driver of energy prices and broader market sentiment.

high.title: Ringgit rises against US dollar ahead of Negeri Sembilan poll
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0830 against the US dollar as easing geopolitical tensions provided some relief, though caution prevails ahead of the FOMC meeting on July 28-29 where a rate hike is increasingly likely. The upcoming Negeri Sembilan state election is also being watched by market participants for potential impacts on national political stability. Both domestic and external factors are creating a complex trading environment for the ringgit.

high.title: Ringgit ends slightly lower amid Middle East tensions, US tariffs
high.summary: The ringgit faced dual pressures from Strait of Hormuz tensions pushing oil prices higher and a new 10% US forced labour-related tariff on Malaysian exports that took effect on July 24. Malaysia's MITI confirmed it will continue engaging with the US over the tariff, which poses a direct threat to Malaysian export competitiveness. These combined external risks are elevating demand for the US dollar and weighing on Asian currencies including the ringgit.

high.title: Bursa Retreats as Market Digests Latest US Tariffs
high.summary: The FBM KLCI faced selling pressure amid new US tariffs, rising crude oil prices above US$100/barrel due to Red Sea attacks and US-Iran tensions, and uncertainty over US tech earnings. Analysts note cautious sentiment but see 1,700 as a key technical support level. This directly impacts Malaysian equity market direction and investor positioning.

medium.title: Defensive stocks lift Bursa at close
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 3.08 points to 1,715.56, driven by consumer products, services, and telecommunications stocks amid cautious sentiment due to Middle East tensions. Iranian missile strikes on US military facilities renewed energy security concerns, keeping broader market gains limited despite gainers outpacing decliners.

medium.title: Bursa rebounds to open higher on improved sentiment
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened 1.91 points higher at 1,714.39 and rose to 1,717.16 by 9.05am on improved sentiment, though upside was seen as limited by the global tech rout. The broader market showed positive early momentum with gainers outpacing losers, signaling cautious optimism among local investors.

medium.title: Ringgit ends higher against most currencies, slips versus US dollar
medium.summary: The ringgit slipped to 4.0885/4.0930 against the USD on July 28 as markets awaited the FOMC outcome, though it gained against other major currencies. Easing crude oil prices on US-Iran negotiation hopes provided some relief, but uncertainty over the Fed's rate guidance kept the ringgit under mild pressure.

medium.title: Kangaroo market is now the new normal
medium.summary: JF Apex Securities describes current global markets as a 'Kangaroo market' with frequent directional swings driven by multiple simultaneous catalysts including Middle East tensions, shipping disruptions, Trump tariffs, Fed policy uncertainty, and slowing Chinese demand. Unlike past single-catalyst events, investors must now monitor multiple shipping routes across the Persian Gulf, Red Sea, Suez Canal, and Mediterranean. This headline-driven volatility is expected to persist for months, posing risks for Malaysian investors with regional and global exposures.

medium.title: Bursa opens lower on cautious stance ahead of FOMC meeting
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened lower at 1,711.95 and eased further to 1,706.33 by 9.15am as cautious sentiment dominated ahead of the FOMC decision. Losers significantly outpaced gainers at 338 to 96, reflecting broad-based weakness across the market. Trading volumes were thin, consistent with a risk-off stance among local and regional investors.

medium.title: Bursa rebounds at open as investors track pause in US airstrikes
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened higher at 1,703.65, gaining 2.63 points as easing geopolitical concerns and softer energy prices encouraged a modest rebound following last week's sell-off. Gainers outpaced losers in the broader market, reflecting cautiously improving sentiment. Malacca Securities noted that investors are refocusing on upcoming Big Tech earnings and the US Fed rate decision as near-term catalysts.

medium.title: Westports Outperforms Despite Middle East Fallout
medium.summary: Westports reported a strong Q2 FY2026 net profit jump of 56% to RM360.9 million and H1 revenue rise of 34% to RM1.76 billion, beating analyst expectations despite a 40% surge in fuel costs driven by Middle East conflict. Container volume dipped slightly by 1% in H1, but profitability remained robust. Multiple research houses maintained 'buy' calls, making this a positive signal for the port and logistics sector.
